text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak will hold talks with Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, who is arriving in Alexandria on Friday. The two leaders will discuss the peace process and bilateral relations during the two-day visit.

- Public Works and Water Resources Minister Abdel Hadi Radi, 59, died in hospital. Radi was admitted into intensive care on Tuesday after he had returned from Paris suffering from severe anaemia. Medical reports said Radi had colon cancer.
- Egypt received offers from Arabs to set up new factories in Sinai as part of the state's plan to attract people to the area, Local Government Minister Mahmoud Sherif said.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri said at the weekly cabinet meeting thatEgypt wanted peace and to raise the standard of living for people in the region.
- Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi will watch the army's live ammunition training exercise.
- The central bank said in a report that state banks' consolidated balance sheets rose to 261 billion pounds in the financial year 95/96, up 24 billion on the previous year.
- Egypt expressed support for the oil-for-food formula which Iraq and the United Nations agreed on. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa described it as "very useful".
- The governors' council confirmed that the situation in flooded areas in the south was under control.
